items.title: Section: The Second Yogic Process Opens — Seventeen Questions

items.zh: 問：於如前所舉、所開示出離地中，有幾品類補特伽羅能證出離？云何建立補特伽羅？云何所緣？云何教授？云何學？云何隨順學法？云何瑜伽壞？云何瑜伽？云何作意？云何瑜伽師所作幾種瑜伽師？云何瑜伽修？云何修果？幾種補特伽羅異門？幾種補特伽羅？幾種建立補特伽羅因緣？有幾種魔？幾種魔事？云何發趣空無有果？
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first part of the second yogic process … Question: Within the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation as already raised and explained, how many kinds of practitioner are capable of realising liberation? How are practitioners classified? What is their object of meditation? What is instruction? What is training? What is conduct in accordance with the training? What is the failure of yogic practice? What is yogic practice? What is mental engagement? What is the yoga master's own work? How many kinds of yoga master are there? What is the cultivation of yogic practice? What is its fruit? How many synonyms are there for a practitioner? How many kinds of practitioner are there? How many causes establish a practitioner as such? How many kinds of demonic force are there, and how many kinds of demonic activity? And what is it to set out towards liberation and yet arrive at no fruit at all?

items.zh: 嗢柁南曰：諸補特伽羅建立、所緣、教、學、隨順學法、壞、瑜伽、作意、瑜伽師、作、修、果、門、數取趣、因、魔事、無果，是皆當廣說。
補特伽羅品類差別有二十八種。云何二十八？謂鈍根者、利根者、貪增上者、瞋增上者、癡增上者、慢增上者、尋思增上者、得平等者、薄塵性者、行向者、住果者、隨信行者、隨法行者、信勝解者、見至者、身證者、極七返有者、家家者、一間者、中般涅槃者、生般涅槃者、無行般涅槃者、有行般涅槃者、上流者、時解脫者、不動法者、慧解脫者、俱分解脫者。
items.en: There are twenty-eight kinds of practitioner. What are the twenty-eight? The dull-facultied; the sharp-facultied; those dominated by desire; by aversion; by delusion; by pride; by discursive thought; those of balanced temperament; those of naturally light affliction; those approaching a fruit; those abiding in a fruit; faith-followers; dharma-followers; those liberated through resolute faith; those who have reached right view; witnesses through direct experience; those bound for at most seven more rebirths; those passing from family to family; those with a single remaining interval; those who attain final nirvana in the intermediate state; those who attain it upon rebirth; those who attain it without further effort; those who attain it through further effort; those who ascend to a higher realm before attaining it; those liberated in due season; those of unshakeable attainment; those liberated through wisdom; and those liberated in both respects.

items.title: Dull Faculties and Sharp Faculties: Innate Temperament and Cultivation

items.zh: 云何鈍根補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，成就鈍根，於所知事遲鈍運轉，微劣運轉，如前已說。此復二種，應知其相。一者、本來鈍根種姓，二者、未善修習諸根。云何利根補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，成就利根，於所知事不遲鈍運轉，不微劣運轉，如前已說。此亦二種，應知其相。一者、本來利根種姓，二者、已善修習諸根。
items.en: What is a dull-facultied practitioner? It is one whose faculties operate slowly and weakly with regard to what should be known, as explained before. This is, moreover, of two kinds: one is dull-facultied by inherent disposition, and one has simply not cultivated the faculties well. What is a sharp-facultied practitioner? It is one whose faculties operate neither slowly nor weakly with regard to what should be known, as explained before. This too is of two kinds: one is sharp-facultied by inherent disposition, and one has cultivated the faculties well.

items.title: Dominated by Desire: How One Craving Becomes Deeply Entrenched

items.zh: 云何貪增上補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於貪煩惱已修、已習、已多修習；由是因緣，今此生中，於所愛事，有猛利貪、有長時貪。是名貪增上補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner dominated by desire? It is one who, in previous lives, has already cultivated, repeated, and extensively practised the affliction of desire; through this cause, in the present life, towards objects of attachment, such a one has fierce desire and prolonged desire. This is called a practitioner dominated by desire.

items.title: Dominated by Aversion, Delusion, Pride, or Discursive Thought

items.zh: 謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於瞋煩惱已修、已習、已多修習；由是因緣，今此生中，於所憎事，有猛利瞋、有長時瞋。是名瞋增上補特伽羅。云何癡增上補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於癡煩惱已修、已習、已多修習；由是因緣，今此生中，於所愚事，有猛利癡、有長時癡。是名癡增上補特伽羅。云何慢增上補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於慢煩惱已修、已習、已多修習；由是因緣，今此生中，於所慢事，有猛利慢、有長時慢。是名慢增上補特伽羅。云何尋思增上補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，於其尋思已修、已習、已多修習；由是因緣，今此生中，於所尋思事，有猛利尋思、有長時尋思。是名尋思增上補特伽羅。
items.en: It is one who, in previous lives, has already cultivated, repeated, and extensively practised the affliction of aversion; through this cause, in the present life, towards objects of hatred, has fierce and prolonged aversion. This is called a practitioner dominated by aversion. … The same applies to delusion … fierce and prolonged delusion. This is called a practitioner dominated by delusion. … The same applies to pride … fierce and prolonged pride. This is called a practitioner dominated by pride. … The same applies to discursive thought … fierce and prolonged discursive thought. This is called a practitioner dominated by discursive thought.

items.title: Section: Balanced Temperament and the Opening of Light Affliction

items.zh: 云何得平等補特伽羅？謂有補特伽羅，先餘生中，雖於貪、瞋、癡、慢、尋思，不修、不習、不多修習，而於彼法未見過患、未能厭壞、未善推求。由是因緣，於所愛、所憎、所愚、所慢、所尋思事，無猛利貪、無長時貪，然如彼事，貪得現行。如貪、瞋、癡、慢、尋思亦爾。是名得平等補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a practitioner of balanced temperament? It is one who, in previous lives, did not cultivate, repeat, or extensively practice desire, aversion, delusion, pride, or discursive thought — yet also never saw their genuine dangers, never developed real revulsion towards them, and never skilfully investigated them. Through this cause, towards objects of attachment, hatred, delusion, pride, or discursive thought, such a one has no fierce or prolonged desire — yet when the occasion for desire actually arises, desire still manifests. The same holds for aversion, delusion, pride, and discursive thought. This is called a practitioner of balanced temperament.

blocks.text: Fascicle 26 opens the **second yogic process** of the Śrāvaka Stage. Having described the path's preparation, the treatise now asks seventeen questions: what kinds of practitioner there are, what they meditate on, how they are taught, and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi: the answers run from this fascicle through fascicle 32. Today: the kinds of person.

How many kinds of practitioner are there? How are they classified? What are the objects of meditation? What are instruction, training, the factors of training, the ruin and accomplishment of yoga, the kinds of yoga, attention, and so on.

Dull and sharp faculties; dominated by desire, aversion, delusion, pride, or discursive thought; balanced; lightly afflicted; approaching and abiding in the fruits; faith-followers and Dharma-followers; and the many kinds of noble person. Master Cháng Bǎi: the dull-facultied are those whose faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are weak.

Dull faculties are of two kinds: by inherent disposition, and from not having cultivated the faculties well. Venerable Miào Jìng: "dull faculties are not fixed; if you are willing to cultivate diligently they will change into sharp ones." And: "sharp faculties come from much experience; experience is wisdom."

One "dominated by desire" has, in previous lives, cultivated desire repeatedly; now, towards attractive objects, desire is fierce and prolonged. Master Cháng Bǎi: if even trivial things arouse strong craving one cannot let go of, that is real greed. The same for aversion, delusion (Venerable Miào Jìng: not knowing that all things arise dependently), pride, and discursive thought.

One who neither cultivated these afflictions in the past nor saw their dangers: no affliction is fierce, but when the occasion comes, each still arises. Venerable Miào Jìng: they never studied the Dharma to counter them.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, which fascicles answer these seventeen questions?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seventeen questions in all, each about the practice of beings, explained from this fascicle 26 through fascicle 29.

quiz.q: How many kinds of practitioner are there, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi define the first, the dull-facultied?
options: twenty-eight; faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are weak and slow, so the noble fruit is not easily attained
quiz.why: "There are twenty-eight kinds of practitioner." Master Cháng Bǎi: the dull-facultied are those whose roots of faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are weak and slow, who cannot easily attain the noble fruit.

quiz.q: Can dull faculties become sharp, according to the two masters?
options: both say yes — with diligent cultivation they turn sharp, called refining or transforming the faculties
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: dull faculties are not fixed; if you are willing to cultivate diligently they will change into sharp ones. Master Cháng Bǎi: through diligent cultivation, dull faculties can become sharp — called refining, transforming, or advancing the faculties.

quiz.q: The note reads "sharp by inherent disposition" as a nature carried over from past-life cultivation. How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: much experience in worldly affairs — experience is wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: sharp faculties come from much experience in worldly affairs — experience is wisdom; if you do nothing at all, your wisdom lags. This is his own reading, differing from the note.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi judge whether desire is fierce and superior-grade?
options: having strong craving even for trivial things, unwilling to let go
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if even trivial things arouse strong craving one cannot let go of, that is true greed — superior-grade fierce desire.

quiz.q: What is "delusion," and how do the masters' emphases differ?
options: Miào Jìng: not knowing that worldly and transcendent things are dependently arisen; Cháng Bǎi: fierce delusion is wrong view, accepted and taught to others
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: delusion in Buddhism means not knowing that both worldly and transcendent things arise dependently. Master Cháng Bǎi: fierce delusion is wrong view — accepting wrong views and teaching them to others.

quiz.q: How do the two masters explain "never skilfully investigated them"?
options: Miào Jìng: never used the Dharma to see and counter these faults; Cháng Bǎi: never skilfully examined the six aspects — meaning, thing, mark, class, time, principle
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: they never studied the Dharma to examine and counter the faults of desire, aversion, delusion, pride, and discursive thought. Master Cháng Bǎi: nor did they skilfully examine the six distinctions of the afflictions' object — meaning, thing, mark, class, time, and principle.
